anomalies.observed: R28 is populated with value "14" even though its library part and description are for 14 kΩ, and the other TMC2209 VREF dividers use 14 kΩ (R24, R26). The SPICE deck also models R28 as 14 Ω.
anomalies.expected: R28 should be 14 kΩ, matching R24/R26, so U7 VREF is approximately 2.16 V rather than nearly 5 V.
anomalies.impact: U7 (Nutrient-B TMC2209) sees a VREF near 5 V instead of ~2.16 V, commanding excessive motor current and potentially overheating or damaging U7 or the Nutrient-B stepper pump.

anomalies.observed: T3 is an AON6407 P-channel MOSFET with its source (pin 2) on the input-side net /+24V_{F} and its drain (pin 3) on the output-side +24V net.
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel reverse-polarity protection MOSFET, the drain should be on the input and the source on the output so the body diode blocks reverse polarity.

evidence.quote: README states the PCB includes "reverse polarity protection, TVS diodes, proper isolation"

anomalies.impact: The board does not block reverse input polarity: reverse input can forward-bias T3's body diode from the +24V rail into the input. Input transients can also overstress T3 gate-to-source voltage because D3 clamps the gate to ground rather than to the source.

parsed.summary: The design contains a clear wrong-value anomaly at R28 (14 Ω instead of 14 kΩ), which would severely overdrive the Nutrient-B TMC2209 current setting. T3's P-channel source/drain orientation also defeats the intended reverse-polarity protection.
